docs.text: Welcome to Fusion! What is Fusion? Fusion is a CLI TCG game that lives in your terminal. You can collect and trade cards with other players, as well as the server. We encourage bots that can make trades and buy from the server and auctions. Why choose Fusion? We know there are lots of TCG's out there, but Fusion is the best choice for a tech-y TCG. docs.text: Cards and Currency Cards Fusion cards all have an ID and some have a name. The id's range from 0 to 65535 - the uint16_t limit. Some cards have a name, whilst other's just an id. The name typically corresponds to something relate to the id. Here are some example cards. Id Name 0 Stdin 1 Stdout 2 Stderr 3 USB 3.0 4 IPv4 5 Raspberry Pi 5 6 Unix V6 7 Windows 7 8 uint8_t 10 OS-X 16 Base 16 - Hex 21 FTP - Port 21 22 SSH - Port 22 23 Telnet - Port 23 64 Commodore 64 80 HTTP - Port 80 84 Ti 84 255 0xFF

docs.text: Connecting You can connect over TCP with Telnet, Netcat or another client. The server address is localhost:23 Connecting with Windows First, you need to install Telnet. If you already have Telnet installed, you can skip this step. Open powershell or command prompt and run: dism /online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:TelnetClient Then, connect to Fusion: telnet localhost 23 Connecting with Mac In order to install Telnet, you need a package manager. The standard MacOS package manager is Brew. If you already have Brew installed, you can skip this step (To check, run brew --version ). Open Terminal and run: /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)" Then to install telnet, run: brew install telnet Now, you can connect to Fusion with: telnet localhost 23 Connecting with Linux In order to install Telnet, you need to install APT, a package manager. You probably already have APT installed. Note for Chromebook users : You need to install the Linux development environment for the Terminal app to work. To check, run in your Terminal: apt --version If the command succeeds, then you can proceed to the next step ( Using APT ). Then, install telnet with APT. apt install telnet You can now connect to Fusion with: telnet localhost 23 Now what? Visit Getting Started to learn how to use Fusion
